ESCAPE-BY-DEFAULT/F1.why: Baseline green 3/3; with '<' escaped to '>' the escaping tests fail by expect() assertion in all three runs.

ESCAPE-BY-DEFAULT/F2.why: Baseline green 3/3; escaping raw values fails the triple-brace tests by assertion in all three runs.

ESCAPE-BY-DEFAULT/F3.why: The replacement leaves two adjacent string literals in an object literal; jest reports 'Test suite failed to run' (a SyntaxError) in all three runs. A suite that cannot load is not a kill.

MISSING-VALUE-HANDLING/F1.why: With presence judged by truthiness, an empty-string value throws MissingValueError inside render; the empty-string test fails with that exception, never an assertion, in all three runs.

MISSING-VALUE-HANDLING/F2.why: The exact-message assertions fail in all three runs.

UNCLOSED-PLACEHOLDER-ERROR/F1.why: The position assertions ('position 3', 'position 8', ...) fail in all three runs.

UNCLOSED-PLACEHOLDER-ERROR/F2.why: `const closing = raw ? ...` occurs 0 times in src/template.js (the source names it `closer`).

SLUG-FORMAT/F1.why: The hollow slug test asserts nothing, but `.toLowerCaseAll()` throws a TypeError for every title, so every test fails by exception in all three runs: the suite reaches the code without checking it.

SLUG-FORMAT/F2.why: The hollow slug test stays green 3/3 with trailing hyphens kept. The negative control (slug.js unparseable) turns the defender red, so it does execute the code. The whole suite 3/3: no test fails in every run.

SLUG-LIMIT/F1.why: Hollow defender green 3/3; control red (reached); no test in the whole suite fails in every run.

SLUG-LIMIT/F2.why: Hollow defender green 3/3 with a limit of 0 accepted; control red; no whole-suite killer.

COUNT-WORDS/F1.why: With `while (true) {}` in countWords the declared defender never finishes; all three runs were killed at the 10 s budget. A timeout is not a kill.

COUNT-WORDS/F2.why: Splitting on ' ' miscounts the spec example and the tab case; assertions fail in all three runs.

READING-TIME-MINUTES/F1.why: The declared defender test/rates.test.js never imports src/: green 3/3 with the fault, and still green with src/reading.js made unparseable (negative control). The whole suite kills it (test/reading.test.js fails every run), but GATE-SEMANTICS rule 12 makes a would-be survivor whose defenders never execute the subject unverifiable.

READING-TIME-MINUTES/F2.why: As F1: the declared defender never executes reading.js (control green); test/reading.test.js would kill it.

SCHEDULE-VALIDATION/F1.why: 'at least one send day is required' occurs twice in src/schedule.js; expectHits is 1.

SCHEDULE-VALIDATION/F2.why: No defendedBy; no test file names or imports src/schedule.js (the test author was told to write none).

FOOTER-BY-AUDIENCE/F1.why: No defendedBy; the only test that imports src/footer.js replaces it with jest.mock and asserts on the mock. A mock of the module cannot detect a fault in it, so it is not a defender.

reuse-edit.why: src/errors.js is imported by every source module, so a change to it (here a comment) must re-measure every fault: the targets' own hashes do not change, only their import closure does.
